summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes, morbid obesity, atrial fibrillation, and prior strokes was admitted for evaluation of rapidly spreading blisters and redness on the left foot. Dermatology diagnosed bullous diabeticorum, and the patient received IV antibiotics as a precaution. A minor procedure was performed to drain a large blister. Despite medical advice to stay overnight, the patient left against medical advice the evening of admission. He was discharged on his home medications with instructions to keep the wound dressing clean and dry and to follow up promptly with outpatient care. No oral antibiotics were prescribed at discharge.
